title: STL reacts to Supreme Court ruling on treatments for trans youth - NewsBreak
text: ST. LOUIS – In a 6-3 vote, the Supreme Court voted to uphold Tennessee’s ban on gender-affirming care for minors on Wednesday. Beth Gasparovic, a parent and president of PFLAG Greater St. Louis, said Wednesday’s ruling by the U.S. Supreme Court is another setback for parents’ rights. “We love our kids,” she said. PFLAG Greater St. Louis is an agency that provides support for parents and grandparents of transgender children. “Taking away that care leaves parents in really just a heartbreaking position to not be able to do for their kids what other parents can,” she said. Thanks for signing up! Watch for us in your inbox. Subscribe Now Missouri Attorney General Andrew Bailey led the fight to ban gender-affirming care in Missouri. He released a statement expressing support for Wednesday’s ruling. “Missouri was the first state in the nation to win on this issue, and the Supreme Court’s decision affirms what we’ve said all along: states have both the right and the duty to protect children from these irreversible and experimental procedures,” Bailey wrote in response to the ruling. Some supporters of the transgender community told FOX 2 that having access to gender-affirming care can be lifesaving. “Imagine being a parent who wants to protect your child and have the freedom to make decisions about your child’s healthcare with them and their doctors and being told no, you don’t have a right to make decisions for your kids,” said Katy Erker-Lynch, executive director of PROMO, an LGBTQ+ public policy and advocacy organization in Missouri. Erker-Lynch said Missouri’s ban has led to some residents leaving the state for states without a ban. Susan Halla is board president of TransParent, a national support agency founded in St. Louis. She plans to leave the state over Missouri’s ban. “What this has done is stripped parental rights from the parents of Missouri,” Halla said. Halla said in some cases families don’t have the resources to move to a state where gender-affirming care is available. “Transgender kids are just like your kid,” she said. “Please see our kids as just kids.” The Metro Trans Umbrella Group provides support for the transgender community in St. Louis. “I’m mostly just worried about how the kids are feeling at this point and time and making sure that they’re ok,” June Choate, the agency’s executive director, said.
